title: Opioid and Controlled Substance Limits in the Pharmacy Benefit
content:
Clinical edit limits applied by each PrairieRx plan of the Pharmacy Benefit.

| PrairieRx plan | Highest daily morphine milligram equivalent (MME) paid without prior authorization | Most days supply of a first opioid fill (no opioid fill in the prior 90 days) | Most refills on one CIII–CV prescription |
|---|---|---|---|
| PrairieRx Dual Wrap | 90 | 7 | 5 |
| PrairieRx Expansion Adult | 90 | 7 | 5 |
| PrairieRx Adult | 90 | 7 | 5 |
| PrairieRx Children | 90 | 3 | 5 |
| PrairieRx Maternity | 90 | 7 | 5 |
| PrairieRx Complex Care | 90 | 7 | 5 |
| PrairieRx Long-Term Care | 90 | 7 | 5 |

### Notes

- The MME ceiling of 90 and the 5-refill ceiling on CIII–CV prescriptions are the same on every plan.
- PrairieRx Children limits a first opioid fill to 3 days supply; every other plan allows 7.

### Reading example (hypothetical)

A first opioid fill written for 5 days supply for a member with no opioid fill in the prior 90 days is within the 7-day figure of PrairieRx Adult and beyond the 3-day figure of PrairieRx Children.
